e: From Swedish ö and Danish ø. Doublet of ey.
From Scottish Gaelic ogha; for spelling see Scots.
q: I love my father's northern land, / Where the dark pine-trees grow, / And the bold Baltic's echoing strand / Looks o'er each grassy oe.
